title: Autonomous mobility gains ground
note: Use historical deployments and explicitly labeled adoption scenarios. The requested exhibit was unavailable. The publisher’s related shared-mobility research supports this as a suggested form.

title: From prompt to purchase
note: Use one row per category and purchase-frequency group. Rank by total and keep the repeat and one-time shares on the same denominator.

title: When electricity costs outpace growth
note: Plot comparable annual growth rates on both axes. Use equal scales, label the parity line, and explain what either side means.

title: Where tech investment could surge
note: Distinguish prior actual, observed half-year and extrapolated full-year. Compare full-year values for the multiple. Never add the observed half-year to the full-year forecast.

title: Beauty’s elusive billion
note: Use counts for each threshold and category. Each dot represents the same count. Thresholds can overlap, so read each panel independently and never sum across them.

title: Energy’s latest chokepoint
note: Use duration on X, peak impact on Y and average disruption for size. Add a separate 100% mix chart for composition. Keep the units and basis visible.

title: AI job losses fall short of forecasts
note: Keep expected and reported outcomes in separate bars. Retain unchanged and uncertain responses and show the survey wave and denominator.

title: Caution crops into farmers’ spending
note: Bind country, survey wave and net spending intent. Use the zero reference and report point changes. The published page confirms the comparisons. Exact exhibit geometry was unavailable.

title: Affordability strains Americans’ aspirations
note: Use separate rankings for overall barriers and cost categories among the subset reporting cost strain. State each denominator next to its chart.

title: Household wealth watch
note: Use consistently valued regional components, one shared unit and period definitions. Distinguish changes in asset prices from net investment in a separate bridge.

title: From likes to buys
note: Plot net trust for each source for two cohorts on equal axes. Keep negative scores and state the sample sizes and net-trust formula.

title: Transparency and trust for AI in nursing
note: Rank survey responses. Show the sample and state that multi-select answers may sum to more than 100%.

title: Human skills in the age of automation
note: Build the ranked curve across all skills and annotate selected percentile points. A separate dot comparison can show named skills. The standard curve supports callouts, while the original overlays a larger marked subset.

title: Stars, stripes, and supply chains
note: Use one row per product with three flags and an exposure measure. Test that all eight combinations reconcile to the total. Circle area is schematic.

title: America powered to compete
note: Stack consumption components and overlay domestic production on the same axis. Use the gap to describe where production exceeds or falls short of consumption.

title: Manufacturing chart collection
note: Start with supplier performance ranges, capacity scenarios or ranked output mix. The link is an index of changing exhibits.

title: The AI advantage in B2B pricing
note: Use one row per activity and technology-horizon pair. Use a shape and color for each pair, and keep survey expectations visually distinct from current use.

title: Trauma’s toll on the workforce
note: Pair the same survey measures for two cohorts and label percentage-point differences. Keep sample sizes and describe results as associations.

title: The aerospace supplier split
note: Use one row per supplier per period and choose the lower and upper percentile. Repeat the layout for each period with comparable axis bounds.

title: AI agents raise cybersecurity stakes
note: Compare budget composition across domains and years. Use 100% bars for share and ranked stacks for absolute spend. Label projected amounts.

title: Scaling smart roads
note: Use one category per technology and a series per adoption stage. Keep stage order consistent and verify that each technology’s responses reconcile.

title: Batteries back the grid
note: Use observed installation and separate scenario series. Sort periods and keep each scenario's assumption and endpoint explicit.

title: AI to browse but not to buy
note: Make separate groups of 100-dot cards for shopping uses and trust. Label the survey question and respondents for each.

title: When populations age
note: Use one pyramid per country or income group and period. Keep age bins and axis scale consistent across panels. State whether the values are counts or shares.

title: Cutting back on quick bites
note: Use signed net intent, zero baseline and separate views by generation or income. Use identical scales and show sample size where available.

title: McKinsey Global Institute: 2025 in charts
note: A collection of exhibits on productivity, trade, technology, climate and demographics. See the Markdown audit for how to reproduce the main forms and where to use a substitute.
